question: Why are electric and magnetic fields in an electromagnetic wave said to be mutually sustaining? Explain briefly.

options.A: The electric and magnetic fields are mutually sustaining because both remain constant during propagation.
options.B: A time-varying electric field produces a magnetic field, and a time-varying magnetic field produces an electric field. In an electromagnetic wave, these changing fields continuously generate each other while propagating.
options.C: Mutual sustenance means that electric and magnetic fields are parallel and have equal magnitudes.
options.D: The fields are mutually sustaining because electromagnetic waves require a material medium to transmit one field into the other.
